_comment: Hardware: qrb5165_flowc -- QRB5165 v66 through Flow C: HTA (CPU_P) + Hexagon v66 DSP (CPU_E) + Kryo 585 CPU (CPU_X), one lane each. Profiles are the tile-level results.csv files flowc/artifacts.py writes from measurements/qrb5165_v66.json.

Periodic taskset -- each model runs at its OWN period, drawn from the model bank's period_ms and snapped to a multiple of the fastest task's (6 ms) so the hyperperiod is just the slowest period (18 ms):
mlp_control: period 6 ms (166.7 Hz), 1 copy(ies), 0.107 ms each (serial on CPU, 1 dispatches), 1.8% of a core, 9 instances over the horizon
mlp_control: window 4 ms (drawn from window_ms 2-8 ms, then fitted to the period; deadline = 35.51x measured runtime), start_time 0 ms
dronet: period 18 ms (55.6 Hz), 1 copy(ies), 0.645 ms each (serial on DSP, 1 dispatches), 3.6% of a core, 3 instances over the horizon
dronet: window 14 ms (drawn from window_ms 5-20 ms, then fitted to the period; deadline = 20.78x measured runtime), start_time 0 ms
Peak backend utilization of the periodic set: 0.04 (budget 0.75) -- CPU 0.02/1, DSP 0.04/1, HTA 0.00/1.
Copies capped by the model bank's max_copies:
mlp_control: 2 copies -> 1 -- copies of a model are concurrent (shared period, back-to-back in the frame), and the bank allows 1 of this one at a time
Horizon 54 ms = 3.0 x hyperperiod; num_instances is ceil(horizon / period) per network, 12 operations in total.
Sporadic tasks placed in the gaps with non-overlapping windows, no edges to the periodic taskset (an edge across the boundary fans out to every periodic instance): (none).

Edges chain the copies of one model, which share its period; models at different rates get none, because workload_factory pairs periodic instances by index and that only means something at equal periods.
No p_core_speedup: it scales only the synthetic-timing fallback, so applying it on top of profiled CSVs would fabricate timings.
dronet: Steering CNN, 1 tile, composes on all three lanes (hta 2.03 ms / dsp 0.645 / cpu 7.00). The baseline arm's mid-size periodic slot.

mlp_control: Control policy, 1 tile. CPU cell is the fp32 context (107.3 us): QnnCpu's int8 path returns a constant for this network regardless of input (measurements/qrb5165_v66.json, _correctness_note in bindings/mlp_control.json). HTA is capability-excluded (elu_s8), so its profile row carries the derived exclusion cost.

ADDENDUM DEVIATION: restrict_makespan_to_nonperiodic set False (the main sweep uses True). With zero non-periodic operations C_max is unconstrained from below, the MILP objective is trivial and MOSEK raises SolverError; the greedy fallback then reports a 0.00 ms non-periodic makespan. Covering all operations makes the objective well-posed and makes the reported makespan the end-to-end makespan of the periodic work, which is the quantity Q1 compares.

CONSEQUENCE: predicted makespans here are NOT comparable to the main sweep's (different objective). The Q1 matched-pair comparison is internal to this addendum -- baseline_seedN vs fused_seedN, same objective, same frozen cost model -- and is unaffected.
